statusText: About an hour after the U.S. cash open and right at the scheduled 14:00 UTC print of preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment (expected ~54.1 vs 55.2 prior), conditions remain calm and largely two-sided. NQ futures have modestly extended a few points above this morning's earlier range high (~30,232) to a fresher read near 30,264 (per a GEX/options-flow snapshot with some timestamp uncertainty), still inside the day's ~140-point band and just under the nearest call-wall resistance cited near 30,300 -- not persistent one-way structure. VIX ticked marginally higher to ~14.63 (range 14.39-14.80), still a calm reading. 2Y/10Y Treasury yields (4.20%/4.68%) and WTI/Brent ($84.77/$93.26) are unchanged from the prior run's Alpha Vantage reads (no fresher daily print available yet). A dated but newly surfaced detail: Iran struck two UAE-flagged ADNOC tankers with drones Thursday evening (minor damage, no injuries), drawing diplomatic condemnation from Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain but no reported military escalation -- this is additional color on the already-priced-in Strait of Hormuz standoff rather than a fresh kinetic step-change, since oil levels are unchanged from the prior run. The actual UMich print is not yet confirmed via available sources. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD, GLOBAL_QUOTE, WTI and BRENT calls succeeded but returned the same stale (1-3 day-old) values as the prior run; MARKET_STATUS failed twice with transient gateway errors and was not retried further. Live VIX, NQ intraday levels, the tanker-attack detail and the UMich calendar context came from WebSearch.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail stays low because NQ itself continues to show no persistent one-way structure -- futures have only modestly extended a handful of points above this morning's earlier high, remain well inside the day's established range, and sit under a nearby options call-wall rather than breaking away from it. Stress holds moderate/elevated into and through the scheduled UMich sentiment print (top of this hour), reflecting the still-unconfirmed data outcome layered on the already-absorbed Retail Sales miss and the newly detailed (but not newly occurring) Hormuz tanker attack; existing-position management and emergency protection remain active through this window regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself following UMich, not the pending confirmation of the print, the standing Hormuz backdrop, or the tanker-attack detail on their own.
headline: NQ futures grind a few points above this morning's range high (~30,264 vs 30,232 prior high) as preliminary UMich consumer sentiment (expected ~54.1) prints at the top of the hour, layering on an already-absorbed July Retail Sales miss (-0.6% MoM); VIX holds calm near 14.63, yields and oil are unchanged from the prior run (4.20%/4.68% 2Y/10Y, $84.77/$93.26 WTI/Brent), and a Thursday-evening Iranian drone strike on two UAE tankers (minor damage, no injuries) adds diplomatic but not military escalation to the standing Strait of Hormuz standoff.
body: At 14:32 UTC, roughly an hour after the U.S. cash open, conditions remain calm and largely two-sided heading into the scheduled preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment release (10am ET / 14:00 UTC, consensus ~54.1 versus 55.2 in July). The actual print is not yet confirmed via available sources at the time of this assessment. July Retail Sales (-0.6% MoM vs +0.1% expected, the steepest drop since May 2025) printed earlier this session and was absorbed with only a modest, mixed cross-index reaction (S&P +0.08%, Dow -0.13%, Nasdaq +0.17%), consistent with the prior run. NQ futures have modestly extended beyond this morning's earlier 30,124-30,232 range, with a GEX/options-flow snapshot showing a level near 30,264 (some timestamp uncertainty on this specific read) -- roughly 30 points, or about 0.1%, above the earlier session high, and still comfortably under a cited nearby call-wall resistance near 30,300 and well above a put-wall near 30,000. This is a mild grind rather than a shallow-pullback or repeated-extension pattern, so it does not constitute observed pathological one-way structure. VIX ticked marginally higher to about 14.63 (range 14.39-14.80 today, opening 14.68), essentially flat and still a calm reading. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD, GLOBAL_QUOTE, WTI and BRENT calls all succeeded this run but returned the identical values already published in the prior run (2Y 4.20%, 10Y 4.68% as of August 12; WTI $84.77, Brent $93.26 as of August 11; QQQ's latest daily close $732.07 as of August 13) -- no fresher print has posted yet on the free tier, so these inputs carry no new information this hour. A dated but newly surfaced detail on the standing Strait of Hormuz standoff: Iran struck two UAE-flagged ADNOC tankers with drones Thursday evening, causing minor damage with no reported injuries; Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain issued formal condemnations, and there is no report of a U.S. or allied military response. Because oil levels are unchanged from the prior run's reads, this is scored as additional detail on the already-priced-in blockade backdrop rather than a fresh kinetic escalation with new market transmission. Alpha Vantage's MARKET_STATUS call failed twice with transient Cloudflare gateway errors and was not pursued further per the economical-use instruction; U.S. cash-session timing is independently well established regardless. Tail holds at 8% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself -- the modest NQ extension is well within a normal range-bound grind, and the Retail Sales miss produced only a contained, mixed cross-index reaction. Stress firms slightly to 42% (moderate) reflecting the still-unconfirmed UMich outcome at the top of this hour layered on the already-absorbed Retail Sales miss, plus the incremental (if not fundamentally new) detail of a confirmed drone strike on two tankers within the standing Hormuz standoff -- a genuine source of residual event uncertainty even though oil itself has not moved. Confidence eases slightly to 52% (medium-low) from the prior run's 58%, reflecting that the Alpha Vantage yield/equity/oil series returned no fresher information this hour, the UMich actual print could not be confirmed via WebSearch at run time, and the specific NQ intraday level carries some timestamp uncertainty from its source.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (8-16%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft CPI/PPI prints; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 51%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and earnings window before easing into the moderate band through Friday's European morning, then firmed back into the low-40s heading into and through today's cash open and Retail Sales miss, with no broader transmission confirmed beyond contained, mixed cross-index reactions.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (2-8%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to hold near its local high in the low-40s through the pending UMich confirmation this hour before easing steadily through the U.S. afternoon into the high-teens by the ~21:00 UTC Friday close/CME weekend halt for NQ. From roughly 22:00 UTC Friday through the end of this forecast window (13:00 UTC Saturday), NQ futures are closed for the CME weekend break (reopening Sunday ~22:00 UTC), so Tail and Stress are held near a low baseline reflecting the absence of active price-path evidence and standing weekend headline/gap risk (principally the Hormuz standoff) rather than any newly observed structure. No forecast slot currently implies an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the low-50s toward the low-30s as the horizon moves away from this run's evidence and, further out, away from any live trading session at all.
